common_name: Reid's Yellow Dent Corn (Historic Foundation Dent Corn)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost once soil is above 55°F, in blocks of at least four rows for reliable cross-pollination; give this tall, vigorous dent corn deep, fertile soil and consistent moisture through pollination and kernel fill.

directions: Sow 1 inch deep in blocks of at least four rows in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, and keep the crop consistently watered through tasseling, silking, and kernel fill for full ears. Reid's Yellow Dent traces to a farm in Illinois in the 1840s and became, through decades of careful ear-to-row selection in the late 1800s, one of the most influential open-pollinated corn varieties in American agricultural history, serving as foundational breeding stock behind much of the hybrid corn later developed across the Corn Belt. It produces tall, sturdy stalks with well-filled ears of smooth, deep-yellow dent kernels, valued for grinding into cornmeal, livestock feed, and general grain use, with a rich flavor typical of good open-pollinated dent corn. Allow ears to dry fully on the stalk, or pull and cure them indoors on a dry rack, before shelling and storing the grain in a cool, dry, rodent-proof container.
